title: Agents on Edge: Deploying LangChain Apps on Cloudflare Workers AI
summary: Karim Lalani shows how to build a LangChain app in JavaScript and deploy it to Cloudflare Workers, with Workers AI serving the model at the edge.
learn: Edge servers sit near population centers around the globe, so an app deployed there loads faster and inference feels closer to real time.
A Cloudflare Worker is a cloud function much like AWS Lambda: scaffold it with npm create cloudflare@latest, test it locally with npm run start, then ship it with npm run deploy.
Values that are safe to commit go under vars in wrangler.toml, while API keys belong in secrets that the Worker reads from env at runtime.
Workers AI hosts open models from the Llama, Mistral, Phi-2, Falcon and Qwen families, plus Whisper for speech to text, Stable Diffusion for images and text embeddings.
The @langchain/cloudflare partner package lacks native tool calling and supports only an older LangGraph, so Lalani published an npm package, tool calling LLM, to add tool use.
The demo chatbot runs on Cloudflare Pages, and Lalani says the Llama model is in beta on Workers AI, so its requests are almost unlimited on the free tier.
